rule.title: Suspicious Scripting in a WMI Consumer
rule.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro

es.summary: Se creó o modificó un consumidor de eventos WMI cuyo campo Destination contiene comandos de PowerShell o scripting sospechosos (descargas, IEX, codificación Base64 o WScript.Shell). Es un patrón típico de persistencia mediante suscripciones WMI.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos Sysmon de consumidores WMI (Event ID 20) donde Destination incluye Net.WebClient con DownloadString/DownloadFile, ' iex(', ' -nop ', ' -noprofile ', ' -enc ', ' -decode ', WScript.Shell o FromBase64Transform.
es.why_it_matters: Las suscripciones WMI (filtro, consumidor y binding) ejecutan código automáticamente ante un evento, como el arranque o un intervalo, sin archivos visibles en carpetas de inicio. Corresponde a ejecución mediante intérpretes de scripts (T1059.005, Visual Basic) y suele usarse para persistencia sigilosa.
triage_steps: Revise Destination, Type (Command Line o Script), Name, Operation y User del evento; decodifique cualquier cadena Base64 o -enc para conocer el payload real.
Busque en el mismo host, +/- 15 minutos, los Event ID 19 (filtro WMI, campo Query) y 21 (binding) para reconstruir la suscripción completa y su disparador.
Identifique el proceso que creó la suscripción (powershell.exe, wmic.exe, mofcomp.exe o un acceso remoto por WinRM/DCOM) y su proceso padre.
Busque procesos hijos de WmiPrvSE.exe o scmrcons.exe en el host para comprobar si el consumidor ya se ejecutó.
Extraiga URLs o IPs del Destination y revise logs de proxy, DNS y firewall para conexiones salientes desde el host.
Compruebe si la cuenta en User es administrativa, si el cambio estaba autorizado y si hay alertas previas para el mismo host o usuario.
false_positives: Scripts administrativos legítimos que registran consumidores WMI para monitoreo o mantenimiento con PowerShell -NoProfile.
Herramientas de gestión de endpoints, inventario o backup que crean suscripciones WMI con scripts VBScript que usan WScript.Shell.
Ejercicios autorizados de red team o pruebas de detección.
response_steps: Verifique con el responsable del host o el equipo de TI si la suscripción es conocida y está documentada.
Si es maliciosa, aísle el endpoint y exporte el filtro, consumidor y binding (Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\subscription) como evidencia.
Elimine el binding, el consumidor y el filtro con Remove-CimInstance solo después de preservar la evidencia.
Bloquee las URLs o IPs identificadas, restablezca las credenciales de la cuenta usada y busque la misma suscripción en otros hosts.
es.severity_rationale: Es alta porque las cadenas detectadas en consumidores WMI casi nunca aparecen en uso legítimo y suelen indicar persistencia activa con ejecución de código.

en.summary: A WMI event consumer was created or modified whose Destination contains suspicious PowerShell or scripting content (downloads, IEX, Base64 encoding or WScript.Shell). This is a common WMI subscription persistence pattern.
en.what_it_detects: Sysmon WMI consumer events (Event ID 20) where Destination includes Net.WebClient with DownloadString/DownloadFile, ' iex(', ' -nop ', ' -noprofile ', ' -enc ', ' -decode ', WScript.Shell or FromBase64Transform.
en.why_it_matters: WMI subscriptions (filter, consumer, binding) run code automatically on a trigger such as boot or a timer, without visible startup entries. This maps to script interpreter execution (T1059.005, Visual Basic) and stealthy persistence.
triage_steps: Review Destination, Type (Command Line or Script), Name, Operation and User; decode any Base64 or -enc string to reveal the real payload.
On the same host within +/- 15 minutes, find Event ID 19 (filter, Query field) and Event ID 21 (binding) to rebuild the full subscription and its trigger.
Identify the process that created the subscription (powershell.exe, wmic.exe, mofcomp.exe or remote WinRM/DCOM) and its parent.
Look for child processes of WmiPrvSE.exe or scmrcons.exe on the host to see whether the consumer has already fired.
Extract URLs or IPs from Destination and check proxy, DNS and firewall logs for outbound connections from the host.
Check whether the User account is administrative, whether the change was authorized, and any earlier alerts for the same host or user.
false_positives: Legitimate administrative scripts registering WMI consumers for monitoring or maintenance using PowerShell -NoProfile.
Endpoint management, inventory or backup tools creating WMI subscriptions with VBScript that uses WScript.Shell.
Authorized red team exercises or detection testing.
response_steps: Confirm with the host owner or IT whether the subscription is known and documented.
If malicious, isolate the endpoint and export the filter, consumer and binding (Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\subscription) as evidence.
Remove the binding, consumer and filter with Remove-CimInstance only after evidence is preserved.
Block identified URLs or IPs, reset credentials of the account used, and hunt for the same subscription on other hosts.
en.severity_rationale: High because these strings in WMI consumers are rarely legitimate and usually indicate active persistence with code execution.

positive.description: CommandLineEventConsumer launching hidden PowerShell with -nop that downloads and runs a remote script
ActiveScriptEventConsumer with VBScript using WScript.Shell to run a binary

negative.description: Legitimate consumer running a local VBScript via cscript without suspicious strings
Consumer running a local PowerShell file with -NoLogo and -File, no download, encoding or -nop flags
